title: Weighted triage & SLA playbook for enterprise data-governance requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket captures a concrete, operational playbook for intake, weighted-prioritization, and SLA commitments for enterprise customer requests related to logging redaction, retention changes, PII handling, and audit exports. The goal is to: 1) create a defensible, repeatable scoring engine that combines data sensitivity, customer tier, legal/contractual constraints, production impact, and exploitability; 2) map score bands to precise routing paths (Legal / Security review / Dedicated ops / Customer Success / Engineering) and SLA buckets; 3) define automation that reduces manual triage and surfaces risks early in the Console; and 4) publish response templates and escalation rules for cross-functional response. This playbook is intended for non-bug requests (policy/configuration) from enterprise customers and should integrate with our intake forms (Zendesk/Intercom), Redwood Console issue creation, and the internal Linear/JIRA workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring sheet exists and is documented with examples for at least 8 common request types (PII redaction, log retention increase, audit export request, GDPR export, data residency override, retention exception, anonymization request, downstream log scrubbing).
Routing matrix implemented as a runnable doc that maps score ranges to owner, SLA, and mandatory approval steps (Legal/Security) and sampled on 10 historical requests for validation.

Automation tasks implemented or prototyped: webhook from intake to create Linear ticket with calculated score, add labels, and assign to correct oncall/queue; test end-to-end for one customer request flow.
Customer-facing response templates and internal runbook published in Confluence with clear handoff checkpoints and measurement dashboards (TTR, escalation rate).
triage_scoring_criteria: Data sensitivity (0-40): public(0), low(5), internal(15), PII/Identifiable(35-40).
Customer tier (0-25): self-serve(0), paid(10), enterprise(20), strategic-enterprise(25).
Legal/regulatory requirement (0-20): none(0), contractual preference(10), legal requirement/complaint(20).
Production impact (0-10): no impact(0), potential dataflow changes(5), active outage/blocked feature(10).
Total score example: PII request from strategic-enterprise with legal requirement -> 40+25+20 = 85 -> falls into 'Immediate Legal Escalation' band.
routing_matrix: Score 0-20 -> Low: Customer Success queue, SLA 10 business days, template: low-priority guidance.
Score 21-50 -> Medium: Product Ops + CS, SLA 5 business days, require Product/Engineering advisory for config changes.
Score 51-75 -> High: Security + Product + CS, SLA 72 hours, Legal consult if contractual language present.
Score 76-100 -> Critical: Immediate Legal + Security + Engineering pager, SLA 24 hours, block/mitigate actions until approved.
automation_tasks: Intake form field additions: data-classification selector, customer-tier dropdown, contract-required toggle.
Webhook that calculates triage score and appends as custom field to Linear ticket + adds 'dg-triage' label.
Console flag to attach request artifacts (SOPs, logs, sample PII) and to redact sensitive attachments automatically.
Daily report that surfaces high/critical requests and SLA breaches to the Compliance Slack channel and weekly digest to GTM leadership.
Template generation: auto-fill customer-facing acknowledgement with expected SLA and next steps.
sample_templates: Acknowledgement (automated): 'Thanks — we've received your request. Based on initial classification your request is [band]. Expected response time: [SLA]. We may request additional info: contract clause, example logs.'
Escalation to Legal (internal note): 'Customer X request involves [data class]. Contract clause: [clause]. Recommended immediate hold on export until Legal signoff.'
Customer closure (if request fulfilled): 'We applied the retention change and confirmed logs were redacted. See artifacts: [link]. Reach out if additional records are needed.'
